scope: General pharmacology vocabulary only. No dosing, purchasing, or medication-use instructions are included.

items.name: Bioavailability
items.summary: The fraction of an administered substance that reaches systemic circulation in an available form.

items.name: Half-life
items.summary: The time required for the measured amount or concentration of a substance to decrease by half under defined conditions.

items.name: Contraindication
items.summary: A circumstance in which a medicine, procedure, or intervention should not be used because the potential risk is considered unacceptable.

items.name: Adverse effect
items.summary: An unwanted or harmful effect associated with a medicine or other intervention.

items.name: Drug interaction
items.summary: A change in effect or exposure that can occur when a medicine is combined with another substance or clinical factor.

items.name: Therapeutic index
items.summary: A conceptual comparison between amounts associated with desired effects and amounts associated with harmful effects.

items.name: Agonist
items.summary: A substance that binds to a receptor and activates a biological response.

items.name: Antagonist
items.summary: A substance that binds to a receptor and reduces or blocks activation by an agonist.

items.name: Clearance
items.summary: A pharmacokinetic measure describing the apparent volume of fluid cleared of a substance per unit time.

items.name: Route of administration
items.summary: The general pathway by which a medicine or intervention is introduced into the body; this entry is definitional and does not provide use instructions.

items.name: Absorption
items.summary: Movement of a substance from its site of administration into the bloodstream.

items.name: Distribution
items.summary: Reversible movement of a substance between the bloodstream and body tissues.

items.name: Drug Metabolism
items.summary: Chemical modification of a substance by the body, often involving enzymes in the liver or other tissues.

items.name: Elimination
items.summary: Removal of a substance or its metabolites from the body.

items.name: Volume of Distribution
items.summary: A proportionality concept relating the amount of a substance in the body to its measured plasma concentration.

items.name: Pharmacodynamics
items.summary: The study of biochemical and physiological effects of substances and how concentration relates to effect.

items.name: Receptor
items.summary: A cellular molecule that can bind signaling molecules or substances and influence a biological response.

items.name: Partial Agonist
items.summary: A receptor ligand that activates a receptor but produces less maximal response than a full agonist under comparable conditions.

items.name: Affinity
items.summary: The tendency of a molecule to bind to a particular receptor or target.

items.name: Potency
items.summary: A concept describing the amount or concentration needed to produce a defined effect; it does not by itself indicate overall benefit or safety.

items.name: Efficacy
items.summary: The maximum biological response that a substance can produce in a defined system.

items.name: First-Pass Metabolism
items.summary: Metabolism that can occur in the intestinal wall and liver before some orally absorbed substances reach systemic circulation.

items.name: Protein Binding
items.summary: Reversible association of a substance with proteins in blood or tissues.

items.name: Steady State
items.summary: A condition in which average input and elimination rates are balanced over time in a repeated-exposure model.

items.name: Drug Tolerance
items.summary: A reduced response to the same exposure after repeated use of some substances.

items.name: Tachyphylaxis
items.summary: A rapidly developing reduction in response after repeated or continuous exposure to some substances.

items.name: Prodrug
items.summary: A compound administered in a form that is converted in the body to an active substance.

items.name: Pharmacogenomics
items.summary: The study of how genetic variation can influence responses to medicines.

items.name: First-Pass Effect
items.summary: Pre-systemic metabolism that can reduce the amount of an orally absorbed substance reaching systemic circulation.

items.name: Enzyme Induction
items.summary: An increase in activity or expression of metabolic enzymes that can alter substance clearance.

items.name: Enzyme Inhibition
items.summary: A reduction in activity of metabolic enzymes that can alter substance clearance.

items.name: Receptor Agonist
items.summary: A ligand that activates a receptor and promotes a biological response.

items.name: Inverse Agonist
items.summary: A ligand that reduces constitutive receptor activity below its baseline level.

items.name: Competitive Antagonist
items.summary: A receptor antagonist that competes with an agonist at the same binding site.

items.name: Idiosyncratic Reaction
items.summary: An unusual and unpredictable response that is not explained by the usual pharmacologic effect.

items.name: Deprescribing Concept
items.summary: A structured clinical process of reviewing and reducing medicines when appropriate under professional supervision.

items.name: Dose–Response Relationship
items.summary: The relationship between the amount or concentration of a substance and the magnitude of a measured biological response.

items.name: Receptor Selectivity
items.summary: The tendency of a substance to affect certain receptor targets more strongly than others.

items.name: Loading Dose Concept
items.summary: A pharmacokinetic concept describing an initial amount designed to approach a target concentration more rapidly; this entry is terminology only, not a dosing instruction.

items.name: Maintenance Dose Concept
items.summary: A pharmacokinetic concept describing repeated or continuous input intended to replace eliminated substance; this entry is terminology only, not a dosing instruction.

items.name: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
items.summary: Measurement and interpretation of selected drug concentrations when clinically appropriate.

items.name: Drug–Receptor Binding
items.summary: Interaction between a drug molecule and a molecular receptor target.

items.name: Saturation Kinetics
items.summary: Nonlinear behavior that can occur when a biological process approaches its capacity.

items.name: Renal Clearance
items.summary: The contribution of kidney processes to removal of a substance from plasma.

items.name: Hepatic Clearance
items.summary: The contribution of liver uptake, metabolism, and excretion to removal of a substance from blood.

items.name: Active Metabolite
items.summary: A metabolite that retains biological activity after a parent substance has been transformed.

items.name: Pharmacovigilance
items.summary: The science and activities related to detecting, assessing, understanding, and preventing adverse effects or other medicine-related problems.

items.name: Medication Reconciliation
items.summary: A structured process for comparing medication information across transitions of care to reduce discrepancies; this is a concept description, not medication advice.

items.name: Precaution
items.summary: A factor requiring additional consideration or monitoring before or during use of a medicine or intervention.

items.name: Drug Excretion
items.summary: Removal of a drug or its metabolites from the body through routes such as urine or bile.

items.name: Therapeutic Window
items.summary: A conceptual concentration or exposure range between insufficient effect and unacceptable toxicity for a medicine; this entry is terminology only.

items.name: Tolerance
items.summary: Reduced response to a substance after repeated exposure, such that the same exposure can produce less effect over time.

items.name: Drug Synergism
items.summary: A conceptual interaction in which combined effects exceed what would be expected from simple addition.

items.name: Additive Effect
items.summary: A conceptual interaction in which combined effects approximate the sum of individual effects.

items.name: Drug Antagonism
items.summary: A conceptual interaction in which one substance reduces or opposes the effect of another.

items.name: Plasma Protein Binding
items.summary: Reversible association of a drug with proteins in plasma, which can influence the unbound fraction available for distribution.

items.name: Blood–Brain Barrier
items.summary: Specialized vascular and cellular barrier properties that restrict movement of many substances between blood and brain tissue.

items.name: Enteral Route Concept
items.summary: Administration through the gastrointestinal tract; this entry describes route terminology and does not provide use instructions.

items.name: Parenteral Route Concept
items.summary: Administration by routes that bypass the gastrointestinal tract; this entry describes terminology only and does not provide procedural instructions.

items.name: Topical Route Concept
items.summary: Application to a body surface for local or systemic exposure; terminology only, not product-use guidance.

items.name: Drug Formulation
items.summary: The physical and chemical form in which a medicinal substance is prepared with excipients for a dosage form.

items.name: Receptor Agonism
items.summary: Activation of a receptor by a ligand that produces a biological response.

items.name: Receptor Antagonism
items.summary: Binding that reduces or blocks receptor activation by an agonist.

items.name: Partial Agonism
items.summary: Receptor activation that produces a lower maximal response than a full agonist in the same system.

items.name: Competitive Antagonism
items.summary: Antagonism in which agonist and antagonist compete for the same or overlapping receptor binding site.

items.name: Steady-State Concentration
items.summary: A state in which the average rate of input and elimination are balanced under defined conditions.

items.name: Receptor Affinity
items.summary: A concept describing the tendency of a ligand to bind to a receptor.

items.name: Intrinsic Activity
items.summary: A concept describing the ability of a receptor-bound ligand to activate a signaling response.

items.name: Drug Potency
items.summary: A comparative concept describing the amount or concentration associated with a defined effect under specified conditions.

items.name: Drug Efficacy
items.summary: The maximal response a drug can produce in a defined biological system.

items.name: Bioequivalence
items.summary: A comparative concept evaluating whether drug products show sufficiently similar exposure under defined study conditions.

items.name: Drug Transporter
items.summary: A membrane transport protein that can influence movement of drugs across biological barriers.

items.name: Ocular Bioavailability
items.summary: The fraction of an applied substance that becomes available at or within ocular tissues under defined conditions.

items.name: Topical Route
items.summary: Administration to a body surface or localized tissue surface.

items.name: Local Drug Delivery
items.summary: Delivery intended to concentrate exposure near a target site rather than throughout the body.

items.name: Mucosal Absorption
items.summary: Movement of a substance across a mucosal surface into local tissue or circulation.

items.name: Tear-Film Clearance
items.summary: Removal of material from the ocular surface through tear turnover and drainage.

items.name: Ion Trapping
items.summary: Differential accumulation of ionizable substances across compartments with differing pH.

items.name: Protein-Binding Displacement
items.summary: Change in the fraction of a bound substance when competition alters binding to carrier proteins.

items.name: Local Tissue Exposure
items.summary: The concentration-time exposure of a substance within a defined local tissue compartment.

items.name: Ocular Surface Residence Time
items.summary: The duration a substance remains available on the ocular surface before clearance.

items.name: Corneal Permeability
items.summary: The capacity of a substance to cross corneal tissue under defined conditions.

items.name: Blood-Retinal Barrier
items.summary: Physiologic barrier properties that regulate movement of substances between blood and retinal tissues.

items.name: Salivary Excretion
items.summary: Transfer of some substances from circulation into saliva.

items.name: Local Mucosal Delivery
items.summary: Delivery directed to a mucosal surface or nearby tissue compartment.

items.name: Tissue Partitioning
items.summary: Distribution of a substance between blood and tissue compartments according to physicochemical properties and binding.

items.name: Compartment Model
items.summary: A mathematical representation that approximates movement of a substance between defined body compartments.
